caption: The drawing is a colored overhead map and illustration labeled "CHEESEBROUGH HOMESTEAD," mainly depicted in greens, blues, browns, and various flower colors. The center of the map features a rectangular blue building with a roof and two small red dots on it, which are surrounded by a green garden bed filled with multicolored patches representing plants or flowers, bordered by a yellow outline. Several rounded green trees of different sizes are scattered throughout the property. At the top of the image is a square, divided garden area with geometric patterns filled with colorful sections in red, yellow, pink, and green, and a circular feature in the center. An oval or circular flower bed with multiple colors appears near the top right with a small brown circular structure or bench adjacent to it. A winding tan-colored path connects various areas, including the entrance to the blue house, the gardens, and the circular area. To the right of the blue building, there’s a triangular garden bed planted with evenly spaced green plants. At the bottom center, a yellow ribbon banner displays the text "CHEESEBROUGH HOMESTEAD." The bottom right corner contains a detailed inset drawing showing a brown wooden gazebo structure covered with green vines and red flowers, topped by a tree canopy. The map also contains a "NORTH" directional arrow on the upper left side and is labeled "from BLACKWELL'S SURVEY" at the top. The background is shaded in green to represent grass or open land.
title: Cheeseborough Estate
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
